analysis.title: "Still The Best AI Hedge": Goldman Doubles Down On The Yen After It Barely Flinched On The Nasdaq's Worst Day Since COVID
key_insights: Goldman's FX strategy team (Kamakshya Trivedi, Karen Reichgott Fishman) maintains that short USD/JPY is the best hedge against an AI bust, despite the yen gaining only about 50bps on Thursday Nov 5 when the Nasdaq 100 fell about 5% by midday.

On that Thursday the DXY was flat, the euro was unchanged, and only the Swedish krona and Aussie moved notably (down 60bps vs USD). Goldman's Noah Gurney said it would be only the 3rd time since 2008 that the broad USD closed within 20bps on such a large risk-off move. It happened 6 times in 2000/01.
Between Oct 9 and Nov 4 the Nasdaq fell roughly 8%, the S&P about 1.5%, 2Y yields about 20bps and 10Y yields about 35bps, yet USD/JPY went nowhere over the month.
Goldman's first defense: since early October USD/JPY fell on average about 0.12% on days the Nasdaq underperformed the S&P 500, and about 0.26% on days of more than 1% underperformance.

The 1-month rolling correlation of USD/JPY daily moves with Goldman's AI basket (GSTMTAIP) rose from about -0.3 in early October to about +0.6, the highest of the year. The prior peak of about +0.5 in July ended when Japan made a record yen intervention.

Goldman's second explanation for flat spot: the yen held up better than its usual beta to yields during the European-led rates selloff from late September to early October, so it had little to give back when yields fell. The gap between USD/JPY and the model opened in late September and closed by early November.

Goldman reads Thursday's drop and Friday's relief as positioning rather than a fundamental downgrade to AI expectations. Outside that day tech moves have been muted, FX vol is low, and Goldman's growth factors for the US, Europe and China show no markdown in global growth.

Goldman says the yen works best as a hedge when the growth outlook deteriorates rapidly, which would be even more true with rising energy prices and a more hawkish Fed. Currently energy is elevated, payrolls printed +165K and the market prices a December Fed hike, so Goldman still sees near-term upside risk for the broad dollar.

Goldman sees the Democratic state-level sweep as slowing data center development in some states, but expects the moratoria to be short-lived since only 7% of voters rank data centers as a top issue. It treats AI as a longer-term valuation risk to the dollar, not a trend change.

Goldman forecasts USD/JPY at 158 in 3 months, 155 in 6 months and 150 in 12 months. The 12-month return for yen longs is 5.1% spot gain, falling to 2.2% after 2.8% negative carry. GSDEER puts the yen about 40% undervalued with fair value at 95.

GPIF's quarterly results through end-September showed domestic bonds at 26.5% of the portfolio and foreign bonds near 24% (about 23% from valuation changes alone). Goldman sees little signal in this and puts the earliest realistic date for an official strategy change at spring 2027.

Per Bloomberg, Japanese investors sold a net ¥1.65 trillion of US sovereign bonds in September, more than triple August's ¥514 billion, and sold the most French bonds in six months. October portfolio flow data is due Tuesday.

The BOJ Summary of Opinions from the Oct 29-30 meeting showed many members see the need for a near-term hike, which puts December in play. The yen fell after the BOJ's September hike because the Fed, ECB and BoE kept out-hawking it. USD/JPY was last near 158.
Goldman's summary: short USD/JPY should work more clearly as a hedge, but it needs a bigger and broader shift in underlying expectations than seen so far.
Per Bloomberg, the Nikkei fell 6% into a bear market on Friday, then rose back above 60,000 on Tuesday after oil fell on US-Iran diplomacy and new AI models revived the trade.
Apollo's Torsten Slok and Capital Economics both argue the dollar depends on the AI trade, since most of the record foreign money in US stocks is unhedged, so a bigger AI bust means a weaker dollar.

trade_ideas.description: Short USD/JPY as a hedge against an AI bust (long yen vs dollar)
trade_ideas.rationale: If AI capex expectations crack, stocks and yields fall together, the US-Japan rate gap narrows and the undervalued yen gains.
trade_ideas.risk: Hedge likely needs a bigger and broader shift in expectations than seen so far. Elevated energy prices and a hawkish Fed argue for near-term dollar upside. The 12-month return is only 2.2% after 2.8% negative carry.

risk_factors: Hawkish Fed (December hike priced), elevated energy prices and a +165K payrolls print support the dollar near term.
Negative carry of 2.8% over 12 months erodes the return on short USD/JPY.
Aggregate AI selloffs may stay too modest to trigger the hedge.
BOJ hike in December may not help the yen if the Fed, ECB and BoE out-hawk it, as after the September hike.
Possible GPIF cut to its foreign allocation would drive repatriation flows, though Goldman sees spring 2027 as the earliest date.
Data center moratoria from the Democratic state-level sweep could slow AI buildout.
vol_and_positioning: FX vol across the majors remains very low, which Goldman cites as a reason the yen has not rallied.
Tech hedge funds round-tripped their entire 2026 gain on Thursday, Nov 5, per the article.
Most of the record foreign money in US stocks is unhedged, per Apollo's Torsten Slok, which links dollar weakness to a bigger AI bust.
Goldman sees the Nov 5 move and Friday's relief as positioning-driven.
geopolitical: US-Iran diplomacy drove oil lower on Tuesday, per Bloomberg, helping a Nikkei rebound above 60,000.
Democratic sweep at the state level raises the prospect of tighter data center regulation and moratoria in key states.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's delta-one desk shares the view that the Thursday drop looked like positioning rather than a fundamental downgrade to AI expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman says USD/JPY has fallen on days tech lagged, the correlation with the AI basket is at +0.6 (highest of the year), the yen is about 40% undervalued, and a bigger AI bust should push it lower.
tension_points.bear_case: The yen barely moved on the Nasdaq's worst day since Covid, and spot was flat over Oct 9 to Nov 4 despite falling yields. The hedge pays only after a broad growth and vol shock. The 12-month return is 2.2% after carry, and Goldman still sees near-term dollar upside risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The hedge needs a bigger and broader shift in AI expectations, including a growth scare, a vol event and a Fed pivot. Without that, the yen stays flat while the Fed, ECB and BoE out-hawk the BOJ.

theme_stances.key_argument: Short USD/JPY should work more clearly as a hedge, but it needs a bigger and broader shift in underlying expectations than seen so far.
theme_stances.evidence: JPY: Still the best AI hedge.
